# distributed-social

> Event-driven Go microservices (accounts, admins, search) that share no
> database and never call each other synchronously -- coordination is
> entirely through a NATS JetStream event stream. Each service owns its
> own Postgres instance and its own SQL migrations.

This file follows the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) convention: a
short, structured entrypoint for language models and coding agents
reading this repository, pointing to the canonical docs rather than
duplicating them.

## Start here

- [README.md](README.md): what this is, quickstart, tech stack, and the
  explicit trade-offs made (eventual consistency, no transactional
  outbox, database-per-service).
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): instructions for AI coding agents -- repo
  layout, hard architectural rules, how to verify a change. Claude Code
  also reads [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md), which just points back here.
- [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md): the event flow between
  the three services, why it's shaped this way, and the full event
  contract table (subjects, publishers, consumers).

## API reference

- [docs/api/accounts.md](docs/api/accounts.md) /
  [openapi/accounts.yaml](openapi/accounts.yaml)
- [docs/api/admins.md](docs/api/admins.md) /

- [docs/api/search.md](docs/api/search.md) /
  [openapi/search.yaml](openapi/search.yaml)

## Source layout

- `internal/<service>/` -- domain logic (models, repository interface +
  Postgres implementation, service with validation/business rules/event
  handling, unit tests against fakes, embedded SQL migrations).
- `api/<service>/` -- HTTP handlers/routes and the `fx` dependency-
  injection wiring that assembles a service's dependencies.
- `internal/eventbus/` -- NATS JetStream wrapper.
- `internal/eventsapi/` -- the shared event contract every service
  imports (subjects + payload structs).
